fields.label: Your story
fields.sample:
We were two students running late for the same class in our first week of university. Outside the door we laughed, “You too?” We missed the class that day, but a friendship began.
Over the years, friendship turned into love, and love into a promise. In front of our families, amid salty coffee and sweet commotion, we said “yes.”
Now we’re putting on our rings and sharing this beautiful beginning with the people we love.

fields.label: Thank-you message
fields.sample:
Thank you endlessly for being by our side on this journey, for sharing our joy and for making this day unforgettable for us.
We’re so glad to have you; here’s to meeting again on many more happy days.

elements.name: Üst başlık
elements.text: Good news · Two families, one table

elements.name: Spot
elements.text: The elders said “by God’s will and the Prophet’s word”; the salty coffee went down with a smile, the chocolates were opened. The engagement will be held before friends and family.

elements.name: Duyuru metni
elements.text:
Dear relatives and cherished friends,
with the consent of our families and the blessing of our elders, our daughter and our son are now engaged. We would be honored to have you with us on this happy day.

elements.name: Hava metni
elements.text: Sunny in the af­ter­noon, with a sweet flurry of ex­cite­ment ex­pect­ed toward evening. A light breeze through the night; spring in every heart. Salt levels in coffee cups will run above sea­son­al norms.

elements.name: Kapak altyazısı
elements.text: The happy couple smiled for our camera shortly before the rings went on.

elements.name: Haber başlığı
elements.text: The salty coffee is drunk, and it’s a “yes”

elements.name: Haber metni
elements.text:
At last weekend’s formal pro­pos­al, the groom-to-be won wide ac­claim by drink­ing the salty coffee he was served down to the last sip with­out so much as a gri­mace. Sources say the bride’s side rated the test “passed with flying colors.”
After a short chat, the family elders spoke the time-honored words “by God’s will and the Prophet’s word”; a moment of si­lence fell over the room, then the ap­plause erupt­ed. As the flow­ers and choco­lates found their owners, the two fam­i­lies were seen swap­ping dessert recipes and old photo albums on the very first evening.
It was an­nounced that the en­gage­ment cer­e­mo­ny will be held with family and close friends. In keep­ing with tra­di­tion, the honor of cut­ting the red ribbon tying the rings will go to the eldest of the family. Word behind the scenes is that the bride-to-be’s mother has al­ready or­dered three trays of bakla­va, while the groom’s father has been re­hears­ing his speech in front of the mirror.

elements.name: Kısa haber
elements.text: The red ribbon that will tie the rings was care­ful­ly taken from the bride’s grandmother’s hope chest.

elements.name: Kısa haber
elements.text: The groom’s side flatly denied claims that some of the choco­lates were eaten on the way.

elements.name: Kısa haber
elements.text: It has emerged that the bride’s sister went un­der­cov­er for three weeks to find out her ring size.

elements.name: Kısa haber
elements.text: Aun­ties are ex­pect­ed up front in every shot; the pho­tog­ra­pher is ad­vised to pack plenty of pa­tience.

elements.name: Kısa haber
elements.text: The good news went up on the building’s notice board that same evening; con­grat­u­la­tions came knock­ing.

elements.name: İlan metni
elements.text: Our door and our hearts are open to your congratulations, prayers and kind words.

elements.name: Telgraf metni
elements.text: Got the news and partied! May your rings bring you luck; we’ll lead the first dance at the wedding.

elements.name: Telgraf metni
elements.text: Congratulations! May your table be full and your home warm. Armfuls of love to our bride.

elements.name: Telgraf metni
elements.text: The minute we heard, we shipped the candied chestnuts. Eat sweet, speak sweet.

elements.name: Telgraf metni
elements.text: Grow old together. If we miss the engagement, we’ll be at the wedding; the dancing’s on us.

elements.name: Sayfa manşeti
elements.text: Two students late for the same class

elements.name: Spot
elements.text: A friendship that began outside a classroom door became, years later, a promise that brought two families to one table.

elements.name: Söyleşi etiketi
elements.text: Interview · One on one with the couple

elements.name: Söyleşi metni
elements.text:
— Who said “hello” first?
Bride: Definitely him. But skipping class for the cafeteria was my idea; I’ve been making the plans ever since.
— What was your first date like?
Groom: We were supposed to study at the library. We talked for three hours and didn’t read a single page. The librarian showed us the door.
— How did the proposal go?
Groom: The coffee was salty, my hands were shaking and my future father-in-law was very serious. Still, it was the best night of my life.
— Who picked the rings?
Bride: We chose them together. My sister secretly got my size; like everyone else, I found out later.
— Each other’s best trait?
Groom: She can laugh at anything.
Bride: His patience. The salty coffee proved it.
— How did the families get along?
Bride: On the first night our moms swapped recipes and our dads talked soccer. We were stuck in the middle.
— Do you ever argue?
Groom: Sure, usually about which show to watch. Whoever has the remote gets the last word.
— What excites you most about the engagement?
Bride: The moment the ribbon is cut. My grandma has been hiding the scissors for months; everyone’s scared of her.
— One promise to each other?
Groom: I’ll make the coffee every morning. No salt.
Bride: And I’ll always drink it with a smile.
— When’s the wedding?
Both: Let’s get through the engagement first, then you’ll read it in our paper!

elements.name: Altyazı
elements.text: From their college years: outside the cafeteria, late for class again.

elements.name: Tarif üst
elements.text: From the kitchen · Just for the groom

elements.name: Malzemeler
elements.text:
1 cup Turkish coffee
1 cup cold water
2 tsp salt (increase to match the groom’s patience)
A pinch of black pepper (optional)
Plenty of smiles

elements.name: Yapılış
elements.text: Stir the coffee and water in the cezve and add salt by eye. Bring to a foam over low heat and pour care­ful­ly into the groom’s cup. Serve with the bride-to-be’s sweet­est smile. Enjoy!

elements.name: Tarif notu
elements.text: Prep: 5 minutes · Serves: 1 groom · Patience: unlimited

elements.name: Gelenek metni
elements.text: The groom’s family ar­rives at the door with flow­ers and choco­lates. First come the pleas­antries and small talk; the real matter is saved for last. Once the coffee is drunk and a si­lence falls, the eldest on the groom’s side clears his throat and says the long-awaited words: “By God’s will and the Prophet’s word…” The bride’s family plays a little hard to get and pre­tends to think it over. The answer usu­al­ly comes with a smile. Then the choco­lates are opened, sweet drinks are served, and from that evening on the two fam­i­lies call each other “in-laws.” With our couple, the words were spoken before the coffee had even cooled.

elements.name: Gelenek metni
elements.text: The bride-to-be brews the coffee with her own hands, but into the groom’s cup goes salt, and some­times pepper. If he drinks it with­out a gri­mace, his pa­tience and love are con­sid­ered proven. The elders say it pre­pares a couple for all the sweet and salty days of mar­riage. In this house, the groom’s cup was drained to the bottom; the bride’s side is pleased. Rumor has it he even asked for a second cup after the last sip. At that moment, the bride’s mother turned to her daugh­ter and said, “This boy really loves you.”

elements.name: Gelenek metni
elements.text: Once the prom­ise is sealed, the rings are tied to­geth­er with a red ribbon and slipped onto the couple’s fin­gers. The eldest of the family cuts the ribbon and wishes them a long and happy life. Pieces of the ribbon are handed out to single guests so that love may find them too. At this en­gage­ment, the ribbon came from the grandmother’s hope chest. The en­gage­ment date and the couple’s ini­tials were en­graved inside the rings; the jew­el­er said he hadn’t seen such an ex­cit­ed couple in a long time.

elements.name: Gelenek metni
elements.text: The groom’s side brings the bride a care­ful­ly pre­pared bundle: fabric, a mirror, a comb, a head­scarf and sweets. As the knot is untied, the women of the family say a prayer and ev­ery­one won­ders what’s inside. In return, the bride’s side sends the groom a shirt, a tie and a hand­ker­chief. In this issue, the exact con­tents of the bundle are being kept secret so as not to spoil the sur­prise. All we can say is this: inside are a hand-embroidered head­scarf and a cup that holds the memory of the salty coffee.

elements.name: Söz
elements.text: “He drank the coffee without a blink. That’s when I said ‘okay.’”

elements.name: Söz
elements.text: “We’d never seen our son talk so excitedly before.”

elements.name: Söz
elements.text: “I’m cutting the ribbon; I’ve already sharpened the scissors.”

elements.name: Söz
elements.text: “I’m the one who got the ring size. Let everyone know.”

A play area has been set up for chil­dren in one corner of the garden. To guests who wish to bring a gift, we gently note that your prayers are the finest gift of all.

elements.text: Ring rehearsal: everything’s ready; all that’s missing is you.

elements.name: Bohça haberi
elements.text:
The groom’s mother has been pre­par­ing the bride’s bundle for months. Ac­cord­ing to leaks from behind the scenes, it holds a silk scarf, a silver mirror, a hand-embroidered head­scarf, a box of Turk­ish de­light and a “first coffee cup.” Word is there’s a little note at the bottom of the cup in memory of the salty coffee. It’s also said that the cloth wrap­ping the bundle is hand­i­work passed down from the groom’s grandmother.
The bundle will be handed to the bride’s mother during the cer­e­mo­ny, and the women of the family will untie the knot to­geth­er. Guests are kindly asked to ac­com­pa­ny the un­wrap­ping with ap­plause. We have also learned that the groom’s side has pre­pared a thank-you gift for the bride’s sister for her “ring-size es­pi­onage.” The color of the shirt the bride’s side will send the groom in return is still a secret.

elements.name: Kıyafet değeri
elements.text: Powder pink, cream and olive green

elements.name: Kıyafet notu
elements.text: Attire is just a suggestion; a smile is the only must.

elements.name: Altyazı
elements.text: The rings are on, the ribbons are cut; now for the blessings.

elements.name: Dua
elements.text: “May God grant you a long life together. May your coffee never lack salt, nor your table flavor; may your home be full of plenty and your hearts of peace.”

elements.name: Fal metni
elements.text: Two birds appear at the bottom of the cup: a jour­ney is coming soon. On the right rim, a big heart; on the left, a crowd­ed table. The grounds have run upward: luck is on its way and will come knock­ing. There’s also a ring, but we knew that al­ready. By the edge of the saucer, good news is ex­pect­ed within three days, weeks or months; most likely the wed­ding date. The wish made as the cup was turned over has come true, if a little salty. In the middle of the grounds, a key can be made out: a new home, a new door. Fi­nal­ly, our fortune-telling auntie looked at the handle and smiled: “Your luck is wide open, and your table will be full.”

elements.name: Mektuplar
elements.text:
“Read­ing our daughter’s en­gage­ment news in a news­pa­per is a feel­ing like no other. We’re fram­ing this issue and hang­ing it on the living room wall.” — Ayten, Kadıköy
“I made the coffee on pro­pos­al day. I con­fess I over­did the salt; our groom still didn’t say a word. Hats off to him.” — The bride’s aunt
“I was always late for that class at uni­ver­si­ty, too. If only I’d been out­side that door that day.” — A classmate
“We’ve kept the mansion’s garden in bloom for thirty years. We saved our finest roses for this en­gage­ment.” — Hüseyin, the gardener
“The day we first met our bride, we un­der­stood why our son was always smil­ing. Wel­come to the family, dear.” — Zeynep
“For years at the cafe­te­ria tea counter, I served the two of them tea sep­a­rate­ly. Turns out they were taking it to the same table.” — Cemal, cafe­te­ria owner
“We can’t wait for your paper’s next issue, the wed­ding issue. Please don’t be late.” — Gülten, next door

elements.name: Sırada metni
elements.text: Date, venue and every detail in Go Post’s special wedding issue. Stay tuned; your invitation is on its way.

elements.name: İlan 1
elements.text: Half of the chocolate box that went missing on proposal day. Finders are kindly asked not to tell the groom.

elements.name: İlan 2
elements.text: The scissors meant to cut the ribbon. Last seen in Grandma’s handbag. A slice of cake to whoever returns them.

elements.name: İlan 3
elements.text: Years of shared memories, a future for two. No haggling, no offers accepted.

elements.name: İlan 4
elements.text: The bride’s childhood bedroom. Old diaries in the closet, high school photos on the shelf. Weekends only.

elements.name: İlan 5
elements.text: As of this date, the groom’s mother will address her daughter-in-law as “my daughter.” For your information.

elements.name: İlan 6
elements.text: Experienced list-keeper wanted for wedding preparations. Must be patient and cheerful.

elements.name: İlan 7
elements.text: From classmates to the happy couple: turns out being late for class had its upside. Best wishes!

elements.name: İlan 8
elements.text: Endless thanks to our sister for secretly getting the ring size. We’ll repay the favor at the wedding.

elements.name: İlan 9
elements.text: Learn to drink salty coffee without a grimace. Instructor: the groom. Limited spots.

elements.name: İlan 10
elements.text: The groom’s soccer jerseys are up for swap to make room for the bride’s novel collection.

elements.name: İlan 11
elements.text: A student ID lost in the cafeteria. Its owner turned up years later; the card is now in the engagement album.

elements.name: İlan 12
elements.text: Guests taking engagement photos are kindly asked to share their best shots with the families.

elements.text: Go Post · Personalized edition · Not for sale, delivered with love
